title: The Stone Maidens
notes: Narration in this story is spoken by the Caryatid (one of the five originals in the museum, speaking for the sisters as 'we'). Each panel carries 'narr_speaker'. Glauka speaks p2.1 and the coda on p3.4.

p3.3: the lettered caption 'Her place on the porch is empty' is wrong today: copies fill all six places on the porch, and the card says so. The gap is in the museum. Narration says so; patch the caption to 'Her place in the museum is empty.'
p1.2, p2.3, p3.4: the same words are lettered in a caption box and a speech bubble (audit 6.3). Patch out the caption boxes if regenerating.
p1.1 and p1.4 show only four maidens: correct for the front row (four in front, two behind). Narration says so.

panels.visual: Six stone maidens (Caryatids) standing in a row as columns of the Erechtheion porch, baskets on their heads supporting the roof, golden light
panels.caption: Six of us hold up the roof of this porch on our heads.
panels.narr: Six of us once held up the roof of this porch, on our heads. No hands. Count the places: four in front, two behind.

panels.visual: Close-up: one Caryatid's carved face slowly opening her eyes, a faint smile, tiny dust falling from her stone lashes
panels.caption: I am a Caryatid.
panels.narr: Yes, the stone is talking. You have to stand very still to hear us. Most people never do.

voice_speech.speaker: Caryatid
voice_speech.text: I am a Caryatid. One of six sisters.

panels.visual: Seen from below, a Caryatid's head and the stone roof resting on it, birds nesting nearby, centuries passing as clock-hands
panels.caption: We have stood here a very long time.
panels.narr: We stood up there for more than two thousand years. Armies came and went. Birds nested on our heads. We held the roof.

panels.visual: Wide shot of tourists and school groups walking under the porch, taking photographs
panels.caption: Everyone looks up at us.
panels.narr: Everyone looks up at us: crowds of faces, little clicking boxes. Nobody asks what we are carrying, or for how long.

panels.visual: Five modern concrete-grey copies of the Caryatids standing on the porch with a sign in the shadow, Glauka pointing at one
panels.caption: The maidens you see outside are copies.
panels.narr: Here's a secret: the maidens you see out here are copies, every one of them. The real sisters moved indoors, down the hill.

panels.visual: Inside the Acropolis Museum: five original Caryatids glowing in a bright hall, protected behind glass, calm
panels.caption: Five of the originals are in the Acropolis Museum, safe from the weather.
panels.narr: Five of us are in the Acropolis Museum now, safe from the weather. Warm, dry, well lit. We hold up nothing at all.

panels.visual: Caryatid close-up shrugging with a stone shrug and a tiny weary eyebrow raised
panels.caption: I do not mind. Much.
panels.narr: Do I miss the porch? The sky, the wind, the roof on my head?

panels.visual: A small group of the Caryatid sisters in the Museum looking sideways with a gentle, grumpy expression
panels.caption: The sisters keep each other company.
panels.narr: Down here, the five of us keep each other company. But look closely at our row. There is a space where a sister should be.

panels.visual: Lord Elgin's men (nineteenth-century Englishmen in tall hats and coats) hauling a statue on ropes and wooden rollers, Greek workers watching
panels.caption: The sixth sister was taken to London by Lord Elgin's men around 1801.
panels.narr: The sixth sister was taken by Lord Elgin's men, around 1801. Ropes, rollers, then a ship to London. Nobody asked her.

panels.visual: A statue of a Caryatid in a grand museum in London with tall windows and foggy weather outside
panels.caption: She is still there.

panels.visual: The empty gap among the Caryatids: five in a row and a dark space where the sixth should stand, a gentle sad atmosphere
panels.caption: Her place on the porch is empty.
panels.narr: Up on the porch, a copy stands in her place now. But down in the museum, beside the five of us, her place is still empty.

panels.visual: The Caryatid sisters in a row, all looking in the same direction, towards the west, with a tear-like drop of rain on one stone cheek
panels.caption: We have been waiting a long time.
panels.narr: That's history: it happened, and you can visit her in the British Museum today. Now go down to the Acropolis Museum and find the gap where she should stand.

voice_speech.speaker: Caryatid
voice_speech.text: We have been waiting. We can wait longer.
